documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for BP/kidneys. Almost a year smoke free, proud of it. Winter cough still there most mornings, white, not worse than last year. No blood. Both COVID shots done.
Meds unchanged, no missed doses. Urinating fine.
Exam: BP and HR as charted. Lungs clear. RRR. No edema.
Imp: HTN controlled. CKD 2, labs today. Smoker's cough lingering after quitting, watch it; CT in November.
RTC for wellness visit in September.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV. Health risk assessment reviewed with patient.
- Tobacco: former, quit 4/2020. Feels his breathing on stairs is better.
- Alcohol: a beer or two a month.
- Activity: walks the dog daily, building a shed for his son-in-law.
- Falls: none. Home safety: ok, grab bar going in.
- Mood: PHQ-2 0.
- Cognition: no concerns from him or wife. Conversation and history fluent.
- Hearing/vision: fine per him.
- Advance directive on file, wife is HCP.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI ~29-30. Heart and lungs normal. Abd soft. No edema.

Personalized plan: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, PSA. Flu and COVID booster at a nurse visit next month. Lung CT in November. Colonoscopy due 2024. Pneumococcal next year. Keep walking.

orders.reason: Chronic productive cough with intermittent blood-streaked sputum, former heavy smoker

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: cough, blood in phlegm.

HPI: 66M, former smoker (40 pk-yr, quit 4/2020). Productive cough for roughly two years now, every winter worse, white sputum most days. Since about December, intermittent blood streaks mixed in, a few times a week. No frank blood, no clots. No fever, sweats, chest pain, weight loss. No new dyspnea. No sick contacts. No blood thinners.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile, sat ok on RA. Lungs with scattered expiratory wheezes, no crackles, no dullness. Heart RRR. No clubbing. No cervical or supraclavicular nodes.

Data: LDCT 11/2021 Lung-RADS 1.

A/P
1. Chronic productive cough with blood-streaked sputum in a former heavy smoker. Last screening CT negative four months ago, reassuring but would like pulmonary to see him. Referral placed. To call if the bleeding increases.
2. HTN/CKD, BMP and UACR today, missed the January visit.
RTC after pulm.

events.reason: Chronic productive cough with intermittent blood-tinged sputum

reports.text: PA and lateral views of the chest. Increased bronchovascular markings bilaterally. No mass. No focal consolidation. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Bony thorax intact.
reports.conclusion: Increased bronchovascular markings without mass or focal consolidation.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary clinic
Date of service: 04/18/2022
Re: Bernard Bennett, DOB 07/03/1955
Referring: primary care

Thank you for asking us to see Mr. Bennett for cough.

He has brought up phlegm most days for about two years, always worse through the cold months. The sputum is white; for roughly the last four months it has been streaked with blood on and off. He has had no fevers, no weight loss and no night sweats.

History: hypertension, chronic kidney disease, BPH, urethral stricture (dilated 2019), lumbar spondylosis. Appendectomy. Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg, acetaminophen as needed. NKDA.
Family: father MI at 68; mother dementia; brother with Paget disease of bone.
Social: retired construction foreman. Former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit in 2020. Rare alcohol.

Exam: BP 135/85, HR 78, SpO2 96% on room air. Overweight gentleman, comfortable. Scattered wheezes throughout with a prolonged expiratory phase. No crackles. Heart regular. No clubbing or edema.

Chest radiograph today, PA/lateral: increased bronchovascular markings; no mass, no focal consolidation.
Screening low-dose CTs 2019-2021 were all negative.

Impression: Chronic bronchitis in a former heavy smoker. The blood streaking fits airway inflammation, and there is no radiographic or recent CT sign of a mass.

Recommendations:
- Remain tobacco free.
- Continue annual low-dose CT screening; next due November.
- Call if he coughs up more than streaks, or with fever or weight loss.
- Follow up with us as needed.

Allergies reviewed: NKDA.
Pulmonary consultant

documents.title: Lung doctor
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw the lung doctor last week. She said chronic bronchitis from all the years of smoking and no tumor on the xray. Do I need to do anything else or come in?

documents.title: RE: Lung doctor
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Got her letter. Agree with her, good news on the x-ray. Nothing new to do: stay off cigarettes, keep the CT in November, and call if the blood picks up. I'll see you for your wellness visit in September.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV + problem.

New: aching in the left leg since about April, hip down into the shin, worse the longer he walks, now some nights too. Tylenol takes the edge off. No injury. Also a few weeks of headaches, dull, and his right ear sounds muffled, wife says he turns the TV up.

Screening: PHQ-2 0. No falls. Independent in all daily activities. Still off tobacco. Memory no concerns.
Cough: usual, no blood since the spring.

Exam: vitals as charted. Ears: canals clear, TMs intact. Left hip: full ROM, no pain with rotation. Left shin feels warm compared to right, no redness today, no focal tenderness. Neuro grossly normal. Heart/lungs ok.

A/P
1. Left leg pain, hip to shin, with a warm shin. Ortho referral to look at the leg with imaging there. Tylenol, no NSAIDs (kidneys).
2. Headache and decreased hearing on the right, new. Will see what ortho finds first, they can arrange a hearing test.
3. HTN, CKD 2: stable on same meds. Labs today.
4. HM: flu, bivalent COVID booster and PCV20 next month. CT in November.
RTC 6 mo.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Three shots today per PCP plan: HD flu L deltoid, bivalent COVID R deltoid, PCV20 L deltoid lower site. No pneumococcal vaccine previously. Tolerated.

events.reason: Left hip and leg pain, headaches, right hearing difficulty

conditions.label: Paget disease of bone, left lower leg

reports.text: AP and lateral views of the left tibia and fibula. The tibial cortex is thickened, with coarsened trabeculae and a patchy cotton-wool appearance of the bone. No fracture. No lytic destruction or periosteal reaction. Fibula normal. Knee and ankle joints preserved.
reports.conclusion: Thickened cortical bone with cotton-wool appearance, left tibia.

reports.text: Pure tone audiometry with air and bone conduction. Right ear: air-bone gap across frequencies, bone conduction thresholds within normal limits. Left ear: thresholds within normal limits without air-bone gap. Tympanometry normal bilaterally.

documents.title: Orthopedic Consultation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Outside orthopedic practice
Visit 10/24/2022
Patient: Bernard Bennett, 67 y/o M

Reason for referral: left leg pain.

Mr. Bennett describes six months of left leg pain that keeps getting worse. He points from the hip down along the front of the shin. More recently he has had headaches and finds he hears less on the right.

PMH: HTN, CKD, BPH, urethral stricture, lumbar arthritis, chronic bronchitis (pulmonary, spring 2022). Former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 2020. Retired construction foreman; occasional alcohol.
Meds: HCTZ 25 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg, acetaminophen PRN. NKDA.
FH: notable for an older brother with Paget disease of bone.

Exam: Left hip moves fully without pain. The left tibia is enlarged and warm to touch with mild erythema; the skin over it is otherwise unchanged. Neurologic exam is unremarkable apart from reduced hearing on the right.

Labs today: calcium 9.8 mg/dL, phosphorus 3.5 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 220 U/L (H), intact PTH 55 pg/mL, 25-OH vitamin D 32 ng/mL.
Radiographs left tibia/fibula: cortical thickening with a cotton-wool pattern.
Audiometry (same day, our audiology): right-sided conductive hearing loss.

Assessment: Paget disease of bone of the left tibia, with a raised alkaline phosphatase and normal calcium, PTH and vitamin D. Right conductive hearing loss.

Plan:
1. Needle biopsy of the left tibia to exclude any other process before treatment; scheduled 11/8.
2. If confirmed, a single zoledronic acid infusion. Please make sure he takes vitamin D and gets enough dietary calcium beforehand.
3. Alkaline phosphatase about 3 months after treatment.

Orthopedic surgery

reports.text:
Specimen: bone, left tibia, needle core biopsy.
Gross: two cores of tan-white bone, 1.4 and 1.1 cm, decalcified.
Microscopic: Thickened, irregular bony trabeculae with a mosaic pattern of cement lines. Increased numbers of osteoclasts, some large and multinucleated, with osteoblastic rimming. Intertrabecular fibrovascular marrow. No atypical cells. No malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Left tibia, needle biopsy: findings consistent with Paget disease of bone. Negative for malignancy.

documents.title: Bone biopsy and pathology
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Outside orthopedics, procedure date 11/08/2022.
Procedure: fluoroscopy-guided needle biopsy, left tibial diaphysis, under local anesthesia and light sedation. Two cores obtained. No complications; discharged home same morning.
Allergies: NKDA.
Pathology (final 11/16): consistent with Paget disease, no malignancy.
Plan: zoledronic acid 5 mg IV, booked at the infusion center for 12/6. Please confirm vitamin D intake.

documents.title: Biopsy and vitamin D
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Bernard, the orthopedic office sent the biopsy result: it shows Paget disease and nothing worse. That's what we hoped for. Before the infusion on 12/6, please start vitamin D 1,000 units once a day (over the counter is fine, I put it on your list) and keep it going afterward. A glass of milk or yogurt and cheese most days covers the calcium. We'll recheck the alkaline phosphatase in late February.

events.reason: Zoledronic acid infusion for Paget disease

medications.sig: 5 mg IV over 15 minutes, single dose

documents.title: Infusion record
documents.author: infusion nursing
documents.body:
Hospital infusion center, 12/06/2022.
Ordering: orthopedics. Dx Paget disease, left tibia.
Pre-check: creatinine within range on 10/24, calcium 9.8. Taking vitamin D 1,000 units daily. NKDA.
Zoledronic acid 5 mg/100 mL IV over 20 minutes, R forearm 22g. No reaction during or after. Discharge teaching: fluids, acetaminophen for aches, report jaw pain.
